Module proof · Mathematics alongside Lean

Exponential response coefficients and their Gram covariances

References and publication status for this development

Published source; corrected checked proofs

The comparison uses the supplied mainDR_dec_18.tex manuscript. The results prove Wasserstein convergence of the kinetic diffusion, invariance of its Gibbs measure, KLMC and KLMC2 error estimates for correlated Gaussian increments, their Cholesky representations, and explicit iteration counts for a prescribed error. The corrected proofs are unpublished. The reference table records the correction to the continuous prefactor and the stochastic Hessian-difference terms retained in the second-order comparison. The KLMC2 estimate retains the exact fourth Gaussian moment in every dimension; the coarser displayed simplification assumes p≥2p\ge2p≥2. The stronger inverse-step-square exponential term is also proved. Continuous solutions are continuous in L2L^2L2 on finite time intervals. Almost-sure continuity of sample paths is not proved here.

  • Arnak S. Dalalyan and Lionel Riou-Durand (2020). On sampling from a log-concave density using kinetic Langevin diffusions. Bernoulli 26(3), 1956–1988. arXiv

For a real friction γ\gammaγ define functions ψk,φk:R→R\psi_k,\varphi_k:\mathbb R\to\mathbb Rψk​,φk​:R→R, k∈Nk\in\mathbb Nk∈N, by

ψ0(t)=e−γt,ψk+1(t)=∫0tψk(s) ds,φ0=0,φk+1(t)=∫0te−γ(t−s)ψk(s) ds.\psi_0(t)=e^{-\gamma t},\qquad\psi_{k+1}(t)=\int_0^t\psi_k(s)\,ds,\qquad\varphi_0=0,\qquad\varphi_{k+1}(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}\psi_k(s)\,ds .ψ0​(t)=e−γt,ψk+1​(t)=∫0t​ψk​(s)ds,φ0​=0,φk+1​(t)=∫0t​e−γ(t−s)ψk​(s)ds.

These are the coefficients of the exponential integrators of Dalalyan and Riou-Durand: the KLMC update (KLMC) uses ψ0(h),ψ1(h),ψ2(h)\psi_0(h),\psi_1(h),\psi_2(h)ψ0​(h),ψ1​(h),ψ2​(h) and the noise covariance ∫0h(ψ0,ψ1)⊤(ψ0,ψ1) dt\int_0^h(\psi_0,\psi_1)^\top(\psi_0,\psi_1)\,dt∫0h​(ψ0​,ψ1​)⊤(ψ0​,ψ1​)dt; the second-order update (KLMC2) adds φ2(h),φ3(h)\varphi_2(h),\varphi_3(h)φ2​(h),φ3​(h) and the four-kernel covariance ∫0h(ψ0,ψ1,φ2,φ3)⊤(ψ0,ψ1,φ2,φ3) dt\int_0^h(\psi_0,\psi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)^\top(\psi_0,\psi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)\,dt∫0h​(ψ0​,ψ1​,φ2​,φ3​)⊤(ψ0​,ψ1​,φ2​,φ3​)dt. Defining ψk\psi_kψk​ by integrals, rather than by closed formulas with powers of γ\gammaγ in the denominator, makes every statement valid for all real γ\gammaγ, including γ=0\gamma=0γ=0.

We prove: continuity and the derivative rules ψ0′=−γψ0\psi_0'=-\gamma\psi_0ψ0′​=−γψ0​, ψk+1′=ψk\psi_{k+1}'=\psi_kψk+1′​=ψk​; the division-free friction identities γψ1(t)=1−ψ0(t)\gamma\psi_1(t)=1-\psi_0(t)γψ1​(t)=1−ψ0​(t) and γψ2(t)=t−ψ1(t)\gamma\psi_2(t)=t-\psi_1(t)γψ2​(t)=t−ψ1​(t) with the resulting closed formulas for γ≠0\gamma\neq0γ=0; a time-scaling identity; values at t=0t=0t=0, nonnegativity, positivity and the bounds ψ0≤1\psi_0\le1ψ0​≤1, ψ1(t)≤t\psi_1(t)\le tψ1​(t)≤t, ψ2(t)≤t2/2\psi_2(t)\le t^2/2ψ2​(t)≤t2/2, ψk(t)≤tk/k!\psi_k(t)\le t^k/k!ψk​(t)≤tk/k! for γ,t≥0\gamma,t\ge0γ,t≥0; the corresponding facts for φk\varphi_kφk​, including φk+1≤ψk+1\varphi_{k+1}\le\psi_{k+1}φk+1​≤ψk+1​, γφ2(t)=ψ1(t)−tψ0(t)\gamma\varphi_2(t)=\psi_1(t)-t\psi_0(t)γφ2​(t)=ψ1​(t)−tψ0​(t) and the exact balance φ2+γφ3=ψ2\varphi_2+\gamma\varphi_3=\psi_2φ2​+γφ3​=ψ2​, which gives φ2≤ψ2\varphi_2\le\psi_2φ2​≤ψ2​ (the paper prints the reverse inequality ψ2≤φ2\psi_2\le\varphi_2ψ2​≤φ2​); and, for Gram matrices Cij=∫0hki(t)kj(t) dtC_{ij}=\int_0^hk_i(t)k_j(t)\,dtCij​=∫0h​ki​(t)kj​(t)dt of continuous kernels, the representation of the quadratic form as an integral of a square and hence positive semidefiniteness for h≥0h\ge0h≥0. 01Definition, continuity and derivatives of the response coefficients §

Mathematical statement and proof

Definition. For γ∈R\gamma\in\mathbb Rγ∈R, define ψk:R→R\psi_k:\mathbb R\to\mathbb Rψk​:R→R recursively by ψ0(t)=e−γt\psi_0(t)=e^{-\gamma t}ψ0​(t)=e−γt and ψk+1(t)=∫0tψk(s) ds\psi_{k+1}(t)=\int_0^t\psi_k(s)\,dsψk+1​(t)=∫0t​ψk​(s)ds, where for t<0t<0t<0 the integral is oriented, ∫0t=−∫t0\int_0^t=-\int_t^0∫0t​=−∫t0​. When the dependence on the friction matters we write ψk(γ)\psi_k^{(\gamma)}ψk(γ)​.

Claim. For every γ∈R\gamma\in\mathbb Rγ∈R and k∈Nk\in\mathbb Nk∈N: (i) ψk\psi_kψk​ is continuous on R\mathbb RR; (ii) ψk+1\psi_{k+1}ψk+1​ is differentiable at every t∈Rt\in\mathbb Rt∈R with ψk+1′(t)=ψk(t)\psi_{k+1}'(t)=\psi_k(t)ψk+1′​(t)=ψk​(t); (iii) ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ is differentiable at every ttt with ψ0′(t)=−γψ0(t)\psi_0'(t)=-\gamma\psi_0(t)ψ0′​(t)=−γψ0​(t).

Proof. (i) By induction on kkk. The function ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ is the composition of the continuous maps t↦−γtt\mapsto-\gamma tt↦−γt and exp⁡\expexp. If ψk\psi_kψk​ is continuous, it is integrable on every bounded interval, and a primitive t↦∫0tψkt\mapsto\int_0^t\psi_kt↦∫0t​ψk​ of such a function is continuous (indeed ∣∫tt′ψk∣≤∣t′−t∣sup⁡∣ψk∣|\int_t^{t'}\psi_k|\le|t'-t|\sup|\psi_k|∣∫tt′​ψk​∣≤∣t′−t∣sup∣ψk​∣ on bounded sets); so ψk+1\psi_{k+1}ψk+1​ is continuous.

(ii) By (i), ψk\psi_kψk​ is continuous, and the fundamental theorem of calculus states that t↦∫0tψk(s) dst\mapsto\int_0^t\psi_k(s)\,dst↦∫0t​ψk​(s)ds is differentiable at every point where the integrand is continuous, with derivative ψk(t)\psi_k(t)ψk​(t).

(iii) By the chain rule, the derivative of t↦e−γtt\mapsto e^{-\gamma t}t↦e−γt is −γe−γt=−γψ0(t)-\gamma e^{-\gamma t}=-\gamma\psi_0(t)−γe−γt=−γψ0​(t). □\square□

Thus ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ is the solution of the friction equation y′=−γyy'=-\gamma yy′=−γy, y(0)=1y(0)=1y(0)=1, and ψk\psi_{k}ψk​ is its kkk-fold primitive vanishing at 000. In the frozen-force integrator, ψ0(h)\psi_0(h)ψ0​(h) multiplies the old velocity and ψ1(h)\psi_1(h)ψ1​(h), ψ2(h)\psi_2(h)ψ2​(h) multiply the frozen force in the velocity and position updates.

How the Lean proof follows this argument

psi γ : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ is defined by recursion on the natural number: psi γ 0 t = Real.exp (-γ * t) and psi γ (k + 1) t = ∫ s in 0..t, psi γ k s, where ∫ s in 0..t, F s is the oriented interval integral. psi_zero and psi_succ restate the two defining equations; both are proved by rfl (they hold by definition) and are marked @[simp] for later simplification.

  1. continuous_psi is (i), by induction k: in the zero case Real.continuous_exp.comp (continuous_const.mul continuous_id) is the continuity of e−γte^{-\gamma t}e−γt; in the succ case intervalIntegral.continuous_primitive gives continuity of the primitive of the function ih, which is integrable on every interval (ih.intervalIntegrable).
  2. hasDerivAt_psi_succ is (ii). HasDerivAt F c t means that FFF is differentiable at ttt with derivative ccc. The proof is the fundamental theorem of calculus intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right, whose three side conditions (integrability, measurability near ttt, continuity at ttt) are all derived from continuous_psi.
  3. hasDerivAt_psi_zero is (iii): ((hasDerivAt_id t).const_mul (-γ)).exp is the chain rule for exp⁡(−γt)\exp(-\gamma t)exp(−γt), and convert … using 1 with simp [psi, mul_comm] matches the form −γψ0(t)-\gamma\psi_0(t)−γψ0​(t).

02Friction identities and closed formulas §

Mathematical statement and proof

Claim. For all γ,t∈R\gamma,t\in\mathbb Rγ,t∈R,

γ ψ1(t)=1−ψ0(t),(1)\gamma\,\psi_1(t)=1-\psi_0(t),\qquad(1)γψ1​(t)=1−ψ0​(t),(1) γ ψ2(t)=t−ψ1(t).(2)\gamma\,\psi_2(t)=t-\psi_1(t).\qquad(2)γψ2​(t)=t−ψ1​(t).(2)

If γ≠0\gamma\neq0γ=0, then

ψ1(t)=1−e−γtγ,ψ2(t)=t−(1−e−γt)/γγ.(3)\psi_1(t)=\frac{1-e^{-\gamma t}}{\gamma},\qquad\psi_2(t)=\frac{t-(1-e^{-\gamma t})/\gamma}{\gamma}.\qquad(3)ψ1​(t)=γ1−e−γt​,ψ2​(t)=γt−(1−e−γt)/γ​.(3)

Proof. (1) By the previous step, s↦1−ψ0(s)s\mapsto1-\psi_0(s)s↦1−ψ0​(s) is differentiable with derivative γψ0(s)\gamma\psi_0(s)γψ0​(s), which is continuous. By the fundamental theorem of calculus (the integral of a continuous derivative is the increment of the function),

γ ψ1(t)=∫0tγ ψ0(s) ds=(1−ψ0(t))−(1−ψ0(0))=1−ψ0(t),\gamma\,\psi_1(t)=\int_0^t\gamma\,\psi_0(s)\,ds=\bigl(1-\psi_0(t)\bigr)-\bigl(1-\psi_0(0)\bigr)=1-\psi_0(t),γψ1​(t)=∫0t​γψ0​(s)ds=(1−ψ0​(t))−(1−ψ0​(0))=1−ψ0​(t),

since ψ0(0)=1\psi_0(0)=1ψ0​(0)=1; the first equality takes the constant γ\gammaγ out of the integral.

(2) Integrate (1), viewed as an identity between continuous functions of sss, over [0,t][0,t][0,t]: by linearity of the integral,

γ ψ2(t)=∫0tγ ψ1(s) ds=∫0t(1−ψ0(s)) ds=t−ψ1(t).\gamma\,\psi_2(t)=\int_0^t\gamma\,\psi_1(s)\,ds=\int_0^t\bigl(1-\psi_0(s)\bigr)\,ds=t-\psi_1(t).γψ2​(t)=∫0t​γψ1​(s)ds=∫0t​(1−ψ0​(s))ds=t−ψ1​(t).

(3) If γ≠0\gamma\neq0γ=0, divide (1) by γ\gammaγ to obtain the first formula; insert it into (2) and divide by γ\gammaγ again to obtain the second. □\square□

Identities (1) and (2) hold for every real γ\gammaγ; at γ=0\gamma=0γ=0 they reduce to 0=00=00=0 and carry no information, while the closed formulas (3) are meaningless. This is why the integral definition is used throughout. In the frozen-force step, (1) and (2) express that the velocity and position responses to a constant force combine consistently with the friction.

How the Lean proof follows this argument
  1. friction_mul_psi_one is (1). hd states that fun s => 1 - psi γ 0 s has derivative γ * psi γ 0 s at every point of uIcc 0 t (the closed interval between 000 and ttt), from hasDerivAt_const and hasDerivAt_psi_zero. hi is the fundamental theorem of calculus intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt; simpa with intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul and psi_succ pulls out γ\gammaγ, identifies ∫0tψ0=ψ1(t)\int_0^t\psi_0=\psi_1(t)∫0t​ψ0​=ψ1​(t) and evaluates ψ0(0)=1\psi_0(0)=1ψ0​(0)=1.
  2. friction_mul_psi_two is (2). he is (1) as an equality of functions (funext); hi integrates both sides over [0,t][0,t][0,t] (congrArg); the rewrites intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul and intervalIntegral.integral_sub split the integrals, and intervalIntegral.integral_const evaluates ∫0t1=t\int_0^t1=t∫0t​1=t.
  3. psi_one_closed and psi_two_closed assume hγ : γ ≠ 0; they use eq_div_iff hγ (a=b/c  ⟺  ac=ba=b/c\iff ac=ba=b/c⟺ac=b for c≠0c\neq0c=0) to reduce to (1) and to (2), the latter after substituting the first closed formula.

03Scaling of the response coefficients under a change of time §

Mathematical statement and proof

Claim. Let c,γ,t,h∈Rc,\gamma,t,h\in\mathbb Rc,γ,t,h∈R with c≠0c\neq0c=0, and k∈Nk\in\mathbb Nk∈N. Then

ψk(cγ)(t)=c−k ψk(γ)(ct),ψk(cγ)(h/c)=ψk(γ)(h)ck.\psi_k^{(c\gamma)}(t)=c^{-k}\,\psi_k^{(\gamma)}(ct),\qquad\psi_k^{(c\gamma)}(h/c)=\frac{\psi_k^{(\gamma)}(h)}{c^k}.ψk(cγ)​(t)=c−kψk(γ)​(ct),ψk(cγ)​(h/c)=ckψk(γ)​(h)​.

Proof. The first identity is proved by induction on kkk, for all ttt simultaneously. For k=0k=0k=0: ψ0(cγ)(t)=e−cγt=e−γ(ct)=c0ψ0(γ)(ct)\psi_0^{(c\gamma)}(t)=e^{-c\gamma t}=e^{-\gamma(ct)}=c^0\psi_0^{(\gamma)}(ct)ψ0(cγ)​(t)=e−cγt=e−γ(ct)=c0ψ0(γ)​(ct). Assume it for kkk and all ttt. Then, by the induction hypothesis and the substitution r=csr=csr=cs (ds=c−1drds=c^{-1}drds=c−1dr, valid for c≠0c\neq0c=0 with either sign, the limits becoming 000 and ctctct),

ψk+1(cγ)(t)=∫0tc−kψk(γ)(cs) ds=c−k c−1∫0ctψk(γ)(r) dr=c−(k+1)ψk+1(γ)(ct).\psi_{k+1}^{(c\gamma)}(t)=\int_0^tc^{-k}\psi_k^{(\gamma)}(cs)\,ds=c^{-k}\,c^{-1}\int_0^{ct}\psi_k^{(\gamma)}(r)\,dr=c^{-(k+1)}\psi_{k+1}^{(\gamma)}(ct).ψk+1(cγ)​(t)=∫0t​c−kψk(γ)​(cs)ds=c−kc−1∫0ct​ψk(γ)​(r)dr=c−(k+1)ψk+1(γ)​(ct).

For the second identity apply the first with t=h/ct=h/ct=h/c, use c⋅(h/c)=hc\cdot(h/c)=hc⋅(h/c)=h and c−k=1/ckc^{-k}=1/c^kc−k=1/ck. □\square□

Multiplying the friction by ccc and dividing time by ccc changes ψk\psi_kψk​ only by the factor c−kc^{-k}c−k. This is the coefficient form of the time change of Lemma 1 of the paper, which reduces a general inverse mass uuu to u=1u=1u=1 by rescaling time and friction by u\sqrt uu​.

How the Lean proof follows this argument
  1. psi_scale has the hypothesis hc : c ≠ 0 and is proved by induction k generalizing t, so that the induction hypothesis ih holds for every ttt. In the zero case simp only and ring compare the exponents. In the succ case simp_rw [ih] inserts the induction hypothesis under the integral, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul extracts c−kc^{-k}c−k, and intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_left is the substitution ∫abF(cx) dx=c−1∫cacbF(x) dx\int_a^bF(cx)\,dx=c^{-1}\int_{ca}^{cb}F(x)\,dx∫ab​F(cx)dx=c−1∫cacb​F(x)dx for c≠0c\neq0c=0; ring collects the powers.
  2. psi_scale_div applies psi_scale at h/ch/ch/c, proves ht : c * (h / c) = h by field_simp, and rewrites c−kc^{-k}c−k as 1/ck1/c^k1/ck with inv_pow and div_eq_mul_inv.

04Initial values, sign and elementary bounds §

Mathematical statement and proof

Claim. Let γ,t∈R\gamma,t\in\mathbb Rγ,t∈R and k∈Nk\in\mathbb Nk∈N.
(i) ψ0(0)=1\psi_0(0)=1ψ0​(0)=1 and ψk(0)=0\psi_k(0)=0ψk​(0)=0 for k≥1k\ge1k≥1.
(ii) If t≥0t\ge0t≥0, then ψk(t)≥0\psi_k(t)\ge0ψk​(t)≥0.
(iii) If t>0t>0t>0, then ψk(t)>0\psi_k(t)>0ψk​(t)>0.
(iv) If γ≥0\gamma\ge0γ≥0 and t≥0t\ge0t≥0, then ψ0(t)≤1\psi_0(t)\le1ψ0​(t)≤1, ψ1(t)≤t\psi_1(t)\le tψ1​(t)≤t and ψ2(t)≤t2/2\psi_2(t)\le t^2/2ψ2​(t)≤t2/2.

Statements (i)–(iii) hold for every real γ\gammaγ.

Proof. (i) ψ0(0)=e0=1\psi_0(0)=e^0=1ψ0​(0)=e0=1, and for k≥1k\ge1k≥1, ψk(0)\psi_k(0)ψk​(0) is an integral over the degenerate interval [0,0][0,0][0,0].

(ii) Induction on kkk, for all t≥0t\ge0t≥0: ψ0(t)=e−γt>0\psi_0(t)=e^{-\gamma t}>0ψ0​(t)=e−γt>0; if ψk≥0\psi_k\ge0ψk​≥0 on [0,∞)[0,\infty)[0,∞), then ψk+1(t)=∫0tψk≥0\psi_{k+1}(t)=\int_0^t\psi_k\ge0ψk+1​(t)=∫0t​ψk​≥0 as the integral of a nonnegative function over [0,t][0,t][0,t] with t≥0t\ge0t≥0.

(iii) Induction on kkk, for all t>0t>0t>0. The case k=0k=0k=0 is the positivity of the exponential. If ψk(τ)>0\psi_k(\tau)>0ψk​(τ)>0 for all τ>0\tau>0τ>0, then on [0,t][0,t][0,t] the function ψk\psi_kψk​ is continuous, nonnegative by (ii), and positive at the point ttt. A continuous nonnegative function that is positive at one point of [0,t][0,t][0,t], t>0t>0t>0, is positive on a subinterval of positive length by continuity, so its integral over [0,t][0,t][0,t] is positive. ψk+1(0)(t)=∫0tskk! ds=tk+1(k+1) k!=tk+1(k+1)!.\psi_{k+1}^{(0)}(t)=\int_0^t\frac{s^k}{k!}\,ds=\frac{t^{k+1}}{(k+1)\,k!}=\frac{t^{k+1}}{(k+1)!}.ψk+1(0)​(t)=∫0t​k!sk​ds=(k+1)k!tk+1​=(k+1)!tk+1​.

The three special cases are k=0,1,2k=0,1,2k=0,1,2.

(ii) We show by induction on kkk that ψk(γ)(t)≤ψk(0)(t)\psi_k^{(\gamma)}(t)\le\psi_k^{(0)}(t)ψk(γ)​(t)≤ψk(0)​(t) for all t≥0t\ge0t≥0. For k=0k=0k=0 this is e−γt≤1e^{-\gamma t}\le1e−γt≤1, proved in the previous step. If it holds for kkk, then for t≥0t\ge0t≥0 the inequality holds at every s∈[0,t]s\in[0,t]s∈[0,t], and integrating over [0,t][0,t][0,t] gives it for k+1k+1k+1. (ii) φ0=0\varphi_0=0φ0​=0 is continuous. (iii) φ0(0)=0\varphi_0(0)=0φ0​(0)=0, and φk+1(0)\varphi_{k+1}(0)φk+1​(0) is an integral over a degenerate interval.

(iv) For k=0k=0k=0 it is trivial. In the second-order scheme, φ2(h)\varphi_2(h)φ2​(h) and φ3(h)\varphi_3(h)φ3​(h) multiply the Hessian correction ∇2f(ϑk)vk\nabla^2f(\vartheta_k)v_k∇2f(ϑk​)vk​ in the velocity and position updates. 09The balance between the second-order coefficients §

Mathematical statement and proof

Claim. For all γ,t∈R\gamma,t\in\mathbb Rγ,t∈R,

∫0te−γ(t−s) s ds=ψ2(t),(1)\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}\,s\,ds=\psi_2(t),\qquad(1)∫0t​e−γ(t−s)sds=ψ2​(t),(1) φ2(t)+γ φ3(t)=ψ2(t).(2)\varphi_2(t)+\gamma\,\varphi_3(t)=\psi_2(t).\qquad(2)φ2​(t)+γφ3​(t)=ψ2​(t).(2)

Consequently, if γ≥0\gamma\ge0γ≥0 and t≥0t\ge0t≥0, then φ2(t)≤ψ2(t)\varphi_2(t)\le\psi_2(t)φ2​(t)≤ψ2​(t).

Proof. (1) Let G(s)=(t−s)ψ1(s)+ψ2(s)G(s)=(t-s)\psi_1(s)+\psi_2(s)G(s)=(t−s)ψ1​(s)+ψ2​(s). By the product rule and ψ1′=ψ0\psi_1'=\psi_0ψ1′​=ψ0​, ψ2′=ψ1\psi_2'=\psi_1ψ2′​=ψ1​,

G′(s)=−ψ1(s)+(t−s)ψ0(s)+ψ1(s)=(t−s) ψ0(s).G'(s)=-\psi_1(s)+(t-s)\psi_0(s)+\psi_1(s)=(t-s)\,\psi_0(s).G′(s)=−ψ1​(s)+(t−s)ψ0​(s)+ψ1​(s)=(t−s)ψ0​(s).

The derivative is continuous, so by the fundamental theorem of calculus and ψ1(0)=ψ2(0)=0\psi_1(0)=\psi_2(0)=0ψ1​(0)=ψ2​(0)=0,

∫0t(t−s)ψ0(s) ds=G(t)−G(0)=ψ2(t)−(t ψ1(0)+ψ2(0))=ψ2(t).\int_0^t(t-s)\psi_0(s)\,ds=G(t)-G(0)=\psi_2(t)-\bigl(t\,\psi_1(0)+\psi_2(0)\bigr)=\psi_2(t).∫0t​(t−s)ψ0​(s)ds=G(t)−G(0)=ψ2​(t)−(tψ1​(0)+ψ2​(0))=ψ2​(t).

The substitution s↦t−ss\mapsto t-ss↦t−s turns the left-hand side into ∫0ts ψ0(t−s) ds=∫0te−γ(t−s)s ds\int_0^ts\,\psi_0(t-s)\,ds=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}s\,ds∫0t​sψ0​(t−s)ds=∫0t​e−γ(t−s)sds, which proves (1).

(2) By the definitions and linearity of the integral, φ2(t)+γφ3(t)=∫0te−γ(t−s)(ψ1(s)+γψ2(s)) ds\varphi_2(t)+\gamma\varphi_3(t)=\int_0^te^{-\gamma(t-s)}\bigl(\psi_1(s)+\gamma\psi_2(s)\bigr)\,dsφ2​(t)+γφ3​(t)=∫0t​e−γ(t−s)(ψ1​(s)+γψ2​(s))ds. By the friction identity γψ2(s)=s−ψ1(s)\gamma\psi_2(s)=s-\psi_1(s)γψ2​(s)=s−ψ1​(s), the bracket equals sss, and (1) gives (2).

Finally, if γ≥0\gamma\ge0γ≥0 and t≥0t\ge0t≥0, then γφ3(t)≥0\gamma\varphi_3(t)\ge0γφ3​(t)≥0 by nonnegativity of φ3\varphi_3φ3​, and (2) gives φ2(t)≤ψ2(t)\varphi_2(t)\le\psi_2(t)φ2​(t)≤ψ2​(t). □\square□

The paper computes φ2+γφ3\varphi_2+\gamma\varphi_3φ2​+γφ3​ in Step 1 of the proof of Proposition 3 and bounds it by t2/2t^2/2t2/2; identity (2) shows that it equals ψ2\psi_2ψ2​ exactly. The chain of inequalities in Step 2 of that proof, 0≤ψ2≤φ2≤φ2+γφ3≤t2/20\le\psi_2\le\varphi_2\le\varphi_2+\gamma\varphi_3\le t^2/20≤ψ2​≤φ2​≤φ2​+γφ3​≤t2/2, has its second inequality reversed; the correct chain is 0≤φ2≤φ2+γφ3=ψ2≤t2/20\le\varphi_2\le\varphi_2+\gamma\varphi_3=\psi_2\le t^2/20≤φ2​≤φ2​+γφ3​=ψ2​≤t2/2, which serves the same purpose in the paper's spectral-norm bound.

10Gram matrices of continuous kernels §

Mathematical statement and proof

Definition. Let ι\iotaι be an index set, (ki)i∈ι(k_i)_{i\in\iota}(ki​)i∈ι​ real functions on R\mathbb RR and h∈Rh\in\mathbb Rh∈R. The Gram matrix of the kernels on [0,h][0,h][0,h] is Cij=∫0hki(t)kj(t) dtC_{ij}=\int_0^hk_i(t)k_j(t)\,dtCij​=∫0h​ki​(t)kj​(t)dt. If WWW is a standard Brownian motion and the kik_iki​ are continuous, the Wiener integrals ∫0hki(t) dWt\int_0^hk_i(t)\,dW_t∫0h​ki​(t)dWt​ are jointly Gaussian with covariance matrix CCC by the Itô isometry; this is the origin of the noise covariances of the paper.

Claim. (i) CCC is symmetric. (ii) If ι\iotaι is finite and every kik_iki​ is continuous, then for every z∈Rιz\in\mathbb R^\iotaz∈Rι

∑i∑jziCijzj=∫0h(∑iziki(t))2dt.\sum_{i}\sum_{j}z_iC_{ij}z_j=\int_0^h\Bigl(\sum_iz_ik_i(t)\Bigr)^2dt .i∑​j∑​zi​Cij​zj​=∫0h​(i∑​zi​ki​(t))2dt.

(iii) If in addition h≥0h\ge0h≥0, then CCC is positive semidefinite: ∑i,jziCijzj≥0\sum_{i,j}z_iC_{ij}z_j\ge0∑i,j​zi​Cij​zj​≥0 for all zzz.

Proof. (i) ki(t)kj(t)=kj(t)ki(t)k_i(t)k_j(t)=k_j(t)k_i(t)ki​(t)kj​(t)=kj​(t)ki​(t) for every ttt, so Cij=CjiC_{ij}=C_{ji}Cij​=Cji​.

(ii) Each function t↦ziki(t)kj(t)zjt\mapsto z_ik_i(t)k_j(t)z_jt↦zi​ki​(t)kj​(t)zj​ is continuous, hence integrable on [0,h][0,h][0,h]. By linearity of the integral (finitely many terms),

∑i,jziCijzj=∫0h∑i,jziki(t)kj(t)zj dt=∫0h(∑iziki(t))(∑jzjkj(t))dt,\sum_{i,j}z_iC_{ij}z_j=\int_0^h\sum_{i,j}z_ik_i(t)k_j(t)z_j\,dt=\int_0^h\Bigl(\sum_iz_ik_i(t)\Bigr)\Bigl(\sum_jz_jk_j(t)\Bigr)dt,i,j∑​zi​Cij​zj​=∫0h​i,j∑​zi​ki​(t)kj​(t)zj​dt=∫0h​(i∑​zi​ki​(t))(j∑​zj​kj​(t))dt,

and the last integrand is the square in the claim.

(iii) By (ii) the quadratic form is the integral over [0,h][0,h][0,h], h≥0h\ge0h≥0, of a nonnegative function, hence nonnegative; together with (i) this is positive semidefiniteness. □\square□

The continuity hypothesis is used only to justify the integrability of the products and the exchange of the finite sum with the integral. Positive semidefiniteness guarantees that a centred Gaussian vector with covariance CCC exists.

  2. gramCovariance_quadratic assumes [Fintype ι] (finite index set) and hc : ∀ i, Continuous (kernels i). hi is the integrability of each term; simp_rw moves the constants zi,zjz_i,z_jzi​,zj​ inside the integrals (← intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, ← intervalIntegral.integral_mul_const); hs and ← intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum exchange the two finite sums with the integral; the remaining pointwise identity ∑i,jzikikjzj=(∑iziki)2\sum_{i,j}z_ik_ik_jz_j=(\sum_iz_ik_i)^2∑i,j​zi​ki​kj​zj​=(∑i​zi​ki​)2 is proved with pow_two, Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum and ring.
  3. gramCovariance_posSemidef (hypothesis hh : 0 ≤ h) concludes PosSemidef. Through Matrix.posSemidef_iff_dotProduct_mulVec this amounts to the matrix being Hermitian (for real matrices, symmetric: Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSymm) and the quadratic form z⋅(Cz)z\cdot(Cz)z⋅(Cz) being nonnegative; he rearranges the double sum, gramCovariance_quadratic rewrites it as an integral of a square, and intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg_of_forall with sq_nonneg concludes.

11The covariance matrices of the two schemes §

Mathematical statement and proof

Definitions. The KLMC kernels are (ψ0,ψ1)(\psi_0,\psi_1)(ψ0​,ψ1​) and the KLMC2 kernels are (ψ0,ψ1,φ2,φ3)(\psi_0,\psi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)(ψ0​,ψ1​,φ2​,φ3​). Their Gram matrices on [0,h][0,h][0,h],

C=∫0h(ψ0,ψ1)⊤(ψ0,ψ1) dt,Cˉ=∫0h(ψ0,ψ1,φ2,φ3)⊤(ψ0,ψ1,φ2,φ3) dt,C=\int_0^h(\psi_0,\psi_1)^\top(\psi_0,\psi_1)\,dt,\qquad\bar C=\int_0^h(\psi_0,\psi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)^\top(\psi_0,\psi_1,\varphi_2,\varphi_3)\,dt,C=∫0h​(ψ0​,ψ1​)⊤(ψ0​,ψ1​)dt,Cˉ=∫0h​(ψ0​,ψ1​,φ2​,φ3​)⊤(ψ0​,ψ1​,φ2​,φ3​)dt,

are the covariance matrices C\mathbf CC and Cˉ\bar{\mathbf C}Cˉ of the paper, which describe the joint law of one coordinate of the (unscaled) noise vector in the KLMC and KLMC2 updates.

Claim. For every γ∈R\gamma\in\mathbb Rγ∈R all six kernels are continuous, and for every h≥0h\ge0h≥0 the matrices CCC and Cˉ\bar CCˉ are positive semidefinite.

Proof. The functions ψ0,ψ1\psi_0,\psi_1ψ0​,ψ1​ are continuous by the first step and φ2,φ3\varphi_2,\varphi_3φ2​,φ3​ by the sixth step. The previous step applies to both finite families. □\square□

Positive definiteness for h>0h>0h>0, which requires linear independence of the kernels on [0,h][0,h][0,h], is proved in a later section; semidefiniteness suffices for the existence of the Gaussian innovations.

  2. continuous_klmcKernels and continuous_klmc2Kernels check each index separately (fin_cases i) using continuous_psi and continuous_phi.
  3. klmcCovariance_posSemidef and klmc2Covariance_posSemidef (hypothesis hh : 0 ≤ h) are direct applications of gramCovariance_posSemidef.

12Entries of the KLMC covariance and the velocity variance balance §

Mathematical statement and proof

Claim. For all γ,h∈R\gamma,h\in\mathbb Rγ,h∈R, the KLMC Gram matrix CCC satisfies

Second, s↦ψ1(s)2/2s\mapsto\psi_1(s)^2/2s↦ψ1​(s)2/2 has derivative ψ1(s)ψ1′(s)=ψ0(s)ψ1(s)\psi_1(s)\psi_1'(s)=\psi_0(s)\psi_1(s)ψ1​(s)ψ1′​(s)=ψ0​(s)ψ1​(s), which is continuous; by the fundamental theorem of calculus and ψ1(0)=0\psi_1(0)=0ψ1​(0)=0, C12=ψ1(h)2/2−0C_{12}=\psi_1(h)^2/2-0C12​=ψ1​(h)2/2−0.

Third, the friction identity with friction 2γ2\gamma2γ gives 2γ ψ1(2γ)(h)=1−ψ0(2γ)(h)=1−ψ0(h)22\gamma\,\psi_1^{(2\gamma)}(h)=1-\psi_0^{(2\gamma)}(h)=1-\psi_0(h)^22γψ1(2γ)​(h)=1−ψ0(2γ)​(h)=1−ψ0​(h)2. The last identity is the stationarity of the velocity update: if vvv has identity covariance and ξ\xiξ is independent with covariance C11IC_{11}IC11​I, then ψ0(h)v+2γ ξ\psi_0(h)v+\sqrt{2\gamma}\,\xiψ0​(h)v+2γ​ξ again has covariance (ψ0(h)2+2γC11)I=I(\psi_0(h)^2+2\gamma C_{11})I=I(ψ0​(h)2+2γC11​)I=I. It holds for every real γ\gammaγ and hhh.
